newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Although he has apologised for throwing his bat after being controversially dismissed in the third Test, the resulting two-match suspension has increased the risk of world-class wicketkeeper Ian Healy being stripped of the cricket vice-captaincy he has trasured since Mark Taylor was appointed to the Australian leadership three years ago. Page 20.

In a ruling handed down on the eve of the Australian Football League premiership, the AFL tribunal suspended Geelong's midfielder Garry Hocking last night for two matches after he pleaded guilty to striking Carlton's Matthew Hogg with an open hand to the face during the Ansett Cup grand final on Friday. Page 20.

Following ongoing negotiations with Stadium Australia, which is overseeing the showpiece Olympic stadium at Homebush, the AFL Commission is confident the Sydney Swans will be playing at the facility by 2001. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following a powerful 41 over performance in the third cricket Test in Pretoria, fast bowler Glenn McGrath, who has been carrying an injured foot since last month, is to return home to Australia this week to rest for the Ashes series against England. McGrath will be replaced by swing bowler Adam Dale. Page 54.

Live coverage of Australia's seven one-day cricket internationals in Saturday will only be shown on pay-TV by Fox Sports, after Channel Seven confirmed yesterday free-to-air viewers will miss out on the live coverage and will only see one-hour highlights ackages. Page 54.

Queensland cricket captain Stuart Law wasted little time yesterday declaring more victory was in store for his side after the Bulls thrashed Western Australia by 160 runs to win the Sheffield Shield final at the WACA Ground. Page 53.
THE AGE

AFL legend Gary Ablett returned to Kardinia Park last night after deciding to return to play for Geelong this year. According to a press release released by Geelong, Ablett says he is "very enthusiastic about the season", yet he has been avidly avoiding te media and has declined to comment on his change of heart. Page B12.

Chris Langford has revealed that although he is keen to continue his AFL career with Hawthorn, his Sydney-based job as a project manager with Lend Lease prevented him training in the summer and he will be unlikely to play until late May or early June - alost halfway through the season. Page B12.

After Ansett Australia's A$1 million-a-year sponsorship deal with the AFL expired last Friday, the League is set to open negotiations with the airline over a new contract for the pre-season competition. The Ansett Cup was again an outstanding success this year. Page B12.
THE HERALD SUN

Twenty-year-old Narabeen surfer Chris Davidson was rescued by lifesavers yesterday after being wiped out by a four-metre wave during the second round of the Rip Curl surfing Pro at Bells Beach. The competition has experienced the biggest conditions since 1981. Page 88.

In a remarkable interview with US Golf magazine just two weeks before he returns to the US Masters in Augusta, Australian golfing legend Greg Norman has revealed he despises some of his fellow players on the US tour, saying they are jealous of him. Page 8.

As Optus Oval's future remains uncertain following the AFL's decision to move to the Docklands facility and keep Waverley Park, Carlton president John Elliott plans to ask Collingwood, Richmond and Essendon to play some of their games at the Optus ground in a bid to secure its future. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

In a decision which follows Chris Caruana's recent racial comments to Owen Craigie, the New South Wales Australian Rugby League board yesterday approved new guidelines aimed at eradicating the sensitive issue of racial and religious vilification in the premiership competition. Page 80.

As Super League yesterday unveiled its uniform for the Super League Tri-series, Canberra Raiders player Laurie Daley predicted the forthcoming series - to be played between New South Wales, Queensland and New Zealand - will have all the intensity of State of Origin matches. Page 80.

Following three consecutive losses and a shared position on the bottom of the ARL competition ladder with Balmain, Western Suburbs coach Tom Raudonikis has held a closed door meeting with his senior players to determine the cause of the club's poor performance. Page 80.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
